author: Mark Atwood
text:
Investigated; both options offered by the bead author plus a third I considered are all trait-API design choices on a published crate (jmap-mail-server 0.1.2). The bead explicitly says 'Either is a deliberate trait-API choice', which fits the workspace AGENTS.md 'two equally-plausible options presented without a recommendation' high-stakes qualifier for filing 'human'.

## Current shape

Three call sites in sieve.rs do get_sieve_blob → size-check → validate_sieve_script in sequence:
- handle_sieve_validate (sieve.rs:1182-1209)
- handle_sieve_set create (sieve.rs:539-562)
- handle_sieve_set update (sieve.rs ~705)

MemoryBackend fetches the blob from the same HashMap in both calls (no observable cost). Production backends fetching from S3 / DB / FS pay 2x I/O.

## Three options on the table

(A) **Modify validate_sieve_script signature** — add `max_bytes: Option<u64>` parameter. Hard break of the existing trait method signature; every SieveBackend implementer must update their impl. Bead's option 1.

(B) **Switch validate_sieve_script to take &[u8]** — handler fetches bytes once, passes them. Cleaner but hard-breaks every implementer, and leaks blob storage details into the handler that the current trait deliberately encapsulates. Bead's option 2.

(C) **Add a new combined method with a default impl** — new `validate_sieve_script_with_size(caller, account_id, blob_id, max_bytes) -> Result<ScriptValidation, Self::Error>` returning an enum (Ok / TooLarge / InvalidSyntax). Default impl orchestrates the current 2-call sequence to preserve behaviour for existing implementers. Production backends override for single-fetch. Strictly non-breaking. (I considered this as the safest middle path; the bead did not list it.)

## Recommendation

Option (C). It's the only non-breaking option, it eliminates the double-fetch for backends that opt in, and existing test fixtures (MemoryBackend, FaultyBackend) keep working with the default impl. Cost: ~50 lines (enum + new method + default impl + 3 call-site updates in sieve.rs).

But this is still a SieveBackend public-API addition on an external-consumer-published crate, and rolling out 3 options for a workspace API decision is exactly the case where the workspace AGENTS.md says to defer to human judgement. Cross-ref the workspace versioning question on JMAP-j7pa.2 — the timing of any SieveBackend addition also depends on the coordinated 0.2 release strategy.

Question for human: (A), (B), (C), or 'defer until the 0.2 bump strategy is set'?
